ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known: the length of line segment $AB=20\text{cm}$, points $C$ and $D$ are two points on line segment $AB$, and $BC=\frac{1}{5}AB$, $AD=\frac{1}{4}AB$. Points $M$ and $N$ are the midpoints of line segments $AC$ and $BD$, respectively. Question: what is the length of line segment $MN$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AB=20cm$, $BC=\frac{1}{5}AB$, $AD=\frac{1}{4}AB$,\\
hence $BC=4cm$, $AD=5cm$,\\
thus $AC=AB-BC=16cm$, $BD=AB-AD=15cm$,\\
as points $M$ and $N$ are the midpoints of line segments $AC$ and $BD$ respectively,\\
thus $AM=\frac{1}{2}AC=8cm$, $BN=\frac{1}{2}BD=\frac{15}{2}cm$,\\
therefore $MN=AB-AM-BN=20-8-\frac{15}{2}=\boxed{\frac{9}{2}cm}$.
